Vancouver, British Columbia – TheNewswire – November 26, 2026 - Femto Technologies Inc. (OTCQB: FMTOF) (“Femto” or the “Company”), a pioneering femtech company, is pleased to report that it now holds 51% of the issued and outstanding common shares of I-Rat Technologies Ltd. (formerly Gilad R.G. Planning and Implementation of Technologies and Software 2025 Ltd.), having exercised the option granted to it under the share purchase agreement signed earlier this year (refer to Femto’s news release of March 27, 2026).

I-Rat Technologies is an Israeli software company focused on the development and sales of advanced, AI-driven research and data analysis solutions with a strategic emphasis on building scalable, software-as-a-service platforms designed for global deployment. Its flagship product, i-RAT (Interactive Researcher Assistant Tool), is an AI-powered SaaS platform designed to guide users across the full lifecycle of quantitative research, integrating statistical learning, hypothesis formulation, data analysis, and automated results reporting into a single, coherent environment.

Femto paid US$250,000 cash to I-Rat Technologies’s shareholder for the additional 11% interest. The purchase price was determined through negotiations rather than by a business valuator. Femto also negotiated a reduction of the amount payable to I-Rat Technologies for the 30% equity interest subscribed for under the original share purchase agreement, from US$1,000,000 to US$750,000.

 

About Femto Technologies Inc.

 

Femto Technologies Inc. (OTCQB: FMTOF) is a cutting-edge femtech company spearheading transformative advancements in wellness technology. With a strong emphasis on AI-driven solutions, Femto is dedicated to innovating products that enhance well-being through intelligent technology integration.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia – TheNewswire – November 26, 2026 - Madoro Metals Corp. (“Madoro” or the “Company”) (TSX VENTURE: MDM; OTC: MSTXF; FSE: A2QQ1X), is pleased to provide a further update regarding the proposed reverse takeover transaction with Narrow River Resources Pty Ltd. (“NRR”) previously announced in the Company’s news release dated February 2, 2026, and as most recently updated in the Company’s news release dated September 29, 2026 (the “Proposed Transaction”).

Madoro and NRR continue to advance the remaining components required under TSX Venture Exchange (“TSXV”) Policy 5.2 – Changes of Business and Reverse Takeovers in connection with the Proposed Transaction. The Company has received comments from the TSXV in connection with its review of the Proposed Transaction. Madoro and NRR, together with their respective advisors, are actively working through those comments and completing the remaining transaction documentation and disclosure materials required to advance the Proposed Transaction.

Subject to completion of the TSXV’s review and receipt of the required TSXV approval, the Company currently anticipates holding the shareholder meeting required to approve the Proposed Transaction during the first quarter of 2027. The meeting date has not yet been fixed and will be announced once the TSXV authorizes Madoro to hold a special meeting in connection with the Proposed Transaction.

Accordingly, the Company has elected to hold its annual meeting of shareholders on December 15, 2026. Shareholders are encouraged to consult the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca for further details.

As previously announced, the Company has entered into a definitive share purchase agreement with 9525-9867 Québec Inc. and NRR in respect of the Proposed Transaction. The parties remain committed to advancing the Proposed Transaction and will provide further updates as appropriate.

 

Considering the revised timing for the Proposed Transaction, the Company and NRR have revised the size and composition of the previously announced concurrent non-brokered private placement (the “Private Placement”), having regard to the anticipated financing requirements of the resulting issuer. The revised terms of the Private Placement are for aggregate gross proceeds of up to C$1,450,000, comprised entirely of hard dollar units (“HD Units”). Under the Private Placement, the Company proposes to issue 29,000,000 HD Units at a price of C$0.05 per HD Unit. There will no longer be any flow-through units offered as part of the Private Placement. Each HD Unit will consist of one common share of the Company (a “Common Share”) and one-half of one common share purchase warrant (each whole warrant, an “HD Warrant”).  Each HD Warrant will entitle the holder to purchase one Common Share at a price of C$0.08 for a period of two (2) years from the Closing. Completion of the Private Placement in connection with the Proposed Transaction will remain subject to TSXV acceptance and all other required regulatory approvals.

 

Completion of the Proposed Transaction remains subject to, among other things, regulatory and shareholder approvals, TSXV acceptance, completion of the Private Placement, finalization and mailing of the Circular, completion of ancillary transaction documentation, and satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.

 

Property Option Amendments

In other news, the Company has entered into a third amendment agreement dated November 26, 2026 (the “Amendment Agreement”) regarding its option to acquire a 100% interest in the First Green Lithium Property in Québec (the “Option”) under the option agreement dated January 31, 2023, as amended on January 18, 2024 and March 1, 2025 (collectively, the “Option Agreement”) (see the Company’s news release dated February 1, 2023 and January 23, 2024 for more details on the Option). The March 2025 amendment extended certain deadlines for the Company to complete the required cash payments and expenditure commitments.

 

Under the Amendment Agreement, the Company will pay the vendors a final payment of C$30,000 in cash on or before December 31, 2026 (the “Final Payment”) in exchange for a waiver of all remaining exploration expenditure commitments under the Option Agreement. As a result of this third amendment, and following completion of the Final Payment, the Company shall have completed the Option, thereby acquiring a 100% interest in the First Green Lithium Property. The Amendment Agreement remains subject to the approval of the TSXV.

Madoro holds an option to acquire a 100% interest in the First Green Lithium Property located in the emerging Décelles lithium camp in the Abitibi Témiscamingue region, approximately 75 kilometers southwest of Val-d’Or, Québec and a 100% interest in the Cerro Minas Property in Oaxaca, Mexico. Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Nations Royalty Corp. (TSXV: NRC) (OTCQX: NRYCF) (FSE: Y96) ("Nations Royalty" or the "Company") is pleased to report financial results for the three and six months ended September 30, 2026.

Financial Highlights

  • Six-months ended September 30, 2026 royalty revenue of C$2.64M and net income of C$0.21M, representing:
    • +382% year-over-year increase in 6 month revenues compared to C$0.55M (1H Fiscal 2026)
  • Second quarter revenues of C$0.43M
    • +21% year-over year increase compared to C$0.36M (Q2 Fiscal 2026)
  • Accrued royalty income in amounts receivable as of September 30, 2026 of C$3.29M
    • Estimate of accrued royalty income for January to September 2026 nine month period
    • Compared to 2025 Brucejack annual payment of C$1.16M
    • Compared to 2024 Brucejack annual payment of C$0.70M
  • Cash and cash equivalents of C$16.7M as of September 30, 2026 with no long-term debt

Nations Royalty is also pleased to announce the appointment of Alex Morrison as Chair of the Board of Directors effective immediately.

Derrick Pattenden, President, CEO and Director of Nations Royalty, commented: "This first half of the fiscal year represents another period of strong year-over-year revenue growth for Nations Royalty and we are pleased to report profitability through the first-half of fiscal year 2027 driven by our royalty on Brucejack. We continue to make meaningful progress with a number of Indigenous communities towards partnering with Nations Royalty on their IBA payments. We view our IBA Advisory practice as a dual engine for growth going forward as successful outcomes lead to increased interest among Indigenous groups in the partnership opportunity presented by Nations Royalty.

I would also like to congratulate Alex Morrison on his appointment as Chair of our Board of Directors. Since the inception of Nations Royalty Alex has been an invaluable source of advice and guidance for the Company, going far beyond the standard expectations of a Director. We are honored to have him as the Chair of our Board of Directors going forward."

Portfolio Update:

Brucejack (Operated by Newmont Corporation):

  • Six-month fiscal year-to-date Brucejack revenues have grown substantially compared to 1H Fiscal 2026 and Nations Royalty remains profitable through the first-half of fiscal 2027.
  • During the three months ended September 30, 2026, management updated its estimate based on additional information provided by Newmont regarding the expected BC Mineral Tax payable for the year. This resulted in lower royalty income recognized in the current quarter relative to the preceding quarter.

KSM (Owned by Seabridge Gold):

  • Seabridge announced on July 20, 2026 that it had entered into an unsecured, short-term loan agreement with a strategic investor for up to US$100 million.
  • Seabridge announced the substantial completion and successful energization of the Treaty Creek Terminal ("TCT") on August 27, 2026. The TCT is a key component of the electrical infrastructure required to support future construction and operations at KSM, and is intended to provide the project with access to hydroelectric power from BC Hydro.
  • On November 19, 2026, Seabridge reported that the Supreme Court of British Columbia had confirmed that its June 8, 2026 ruling quashed the KSM Project's substantially started designation pending the EAO's reconsideration, but that the KSM environmental assessment certificate is not affected.
  • On November 23, 2026, the Nisga'a Nation and the Tahltan Nation publicly stated their support for the KSM Project and its substantially started designation.

Premier and Red Mountain (Owned by Cambria Gold Mines):

  • Received final permits for and commenced construction on the access road to the Red Mountain Gold Deposit, the completion of which represents a key step towards production.
  • Cambria is targeting road access to the base of Red Mountain through the end of 2026.
  • Targeting completion of an updated combined Red Mountain-Premier Feasibility study in the first-half of 2027.
  • Targeting commissioning of the 2,500 tonne-per-day mill at Premier in Q4 2027.

Outlook

Nations Royalty maintains a strong financial position including C$16.7 million of cash and cash equivalents and no long-term debt.

The Company believes its diversified portfolio of producing and development-stage Indigenous royalty interests is well positioned to benefit from strength in precious metals markets and the advancement of several large-scale mining projects across northwestern British Columbia, Canada.

Management remains focused on creating value for shareholders and Indigenous partners by:

  • Expanding the Company's portfolio through partnerships with Indigenous Nations;
  • Acquiring additional high-quality royalty interests; and
  • Maintaining disciplined capital allocation.

As Canada's first majority Indigenous-owned publicly listed royalty company, Nations Royalty believes its differentiated partnership model positions it to become the preferred long-term royalty partner for Indigenous Nations participating in Canada's mining industry.

Stock Options

The Company also announces that it has granted 125,000 incentive stock options to its Director, Investor Relations, exercisable at $0.82 per share for a period of five (5) years from the date of grant. The options vest in stages over three years in accordance with the Company's stock option plan and are subject to TSXV approval.

About Nations Royalty Corp.

The Company's vision is to unite First Nations and Indigenous groups across Canada, welcoming external investors to join the Company as shareholders. Together, they will combine royalties, income and commodity streams and annual benefit payment entitlements from resource projects, tapping into the growth, diversification and value potential typical of publicly traded royalty companies. As a leader in the spirit of economic reconciliation, Nations Royalty's mission includes capacity building of Indigenous People in public companies and capital markets.

Nations Royalty's foundation begins with five annual benefit payment entitlements in place in respect of the following properties in Canada:

  • The high-grade Brucejack gold mine operated by Newmont Corporation;
  • The KSM Copper-Gold-Silver-Molybdenum deposit, currently in development by Seabridge Gold Inc.;
  • The Premier Gold Project, currently evaluating a restart decision by Cambria Gold Mines Inc.;
  • The Red Mountain Gold Deposit, owned by Cambria Gold Mines Inc.; and
  • The Kitsault Molybdenum Deposit, a large, fully permitted brownfield site owned and being actively advanced by New Moly LLC, majority-owned by Resource Capital Fund VI L.P.

An electric bus partnership in the U.S. and expanded sales and service options for drivers show how VinFast is putting its electric mobility strategy into practice. The company's published climate roadmap outlines how it plans to reduce emissions as the business grows.

IRVINE, Calif., Nov. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- While some automakers have scaled back their North American EV ambitions, VinFast continues to view electric vehicles as essential to addressing climate change. In the U.S. and Canada, the company is focused on making EVs easier to purchase, charge and service while helping customers understand operating costs. Its broader strategy centers on building a network of vehicles, charging infrastructure and services that can support more drivers and fleets over time.

One of the latest steps came on October 6, 2026, when VinFast announced an initial agreement with NexMove at the APTA TRANSform & EXPO in Chicago to bring its electric buses to U.S. customers. NexMove, a joint venture between Transportation Management Services and Zeem Solutions, plans to bundle buses, charging, maintenance and operations in a single agreement. It intends to offer a 97% uptime service-level commitment, with certified bus deliveries expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028. The announcement followed VinFast's September 2026 franchise agreements for three U.S. dealerships in California and Pennsylvania.

Making electric mobility practical for fleets and drivers

For a transit agency, introducing electric buses requires decisions about depot charging, maintenance schedules and daily vehicle availability. NexMove's proposed service brings these elements together into one agreement. Ahead of certified deliveries, NexMove plans to place demonstration buses at Zeem's charging depots, where transit agencies and fleet operators can evaluate the vehicles firsthand. The demonstration units are intended for evaluation, with certified vehicles to follow on the planned delivery schedule. 

VinFast's buses combine camera- and radar-based driver assistance, fast charging capabilities, lithium iron phosphate batteries and corrosion protection. The company reported that approximately 2,000 of its electric buses were operating in Vietnam at the time of the announcement. VinFast's experience in the market spans manufacturing, operations and maintenance, giving it firsthand knowledge of the demands fleet operators face when vehicles are in daily service. 

"Bringing VinFast electric buses to the United States marks an important next step in our long-term commitment to this market," said Brian Finnerty, CEO of VinFast North America. 

For households, the questions are more personal: How much will it cost to charge a vehicle each month? Where can it be serviced? What options are available at a price the buyer can afford? The franchise agreements in Redondo Beach and Tustin, California, and Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, expand access to sales and after-sales service. The company's U.S. certified pre-owned program gives buyers another option when weighing the upfront cost of an EV.

In Canada, VinFast offers a 10-year or 200,000-kilometre limited new-vehicle warranty on the VF 8, whichever comes first. Its online energy-cost calculator allows shoppers to compare estimated EV charging costs with the fueling costs of a gasoline vehicle over their expected mileage and ownership period. The comparison gives buyers a clearer picture of how an EV could fit their driving habits and household budget.

Annual EV charging costs can be 50% or more below gasoline fueling costs, depending on electricity rates, whether drivers charge at home or use public stations, driving habits, and vehicle efficiency. Coltura's Q3 2024 analysis estimated that U.S. EV drivers saved an average of 7.4 cents per mile on fuel. At 1,200 miles a month, that works out to about $90 a month, or nearly $1,100 a year if the same per-mile savings hold.

Why a long-term climate commitment matters as markets change

VinFast announced its transition to all-electric vehicle production at CES in Las Vegas in 2022. Just over two years later, it became Vietnam's best-selling vehicle brand in 2024, according to Vingroup's annual report. Its expansion into North America brings a different set of considerations, including where to build out sales and service operations, how to support charging infrastructure and how to help commercial customers integrate electric vehicles into their existing operations. 

Incentives, regulations and customer demand can change while a factory upgrade or charging project is still in development. VinFast's 2040 net-zero goal provides a long-term framework for investments that take years to plan and implement. For example, the timing of an equipment replacement affects when a plant can shift more of its operations to electricity. The source of that electricity then affects the emissions associated with running the equipment. Decisions about materials and suppliers have a similar bearing on emissions across the value chain. 

VinFast's emissions inventory illustrates why those decisions matter as production grows. The company calculated that its emissions exceeded 1.12 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) in its 2022 base year. In a separate scenario, VinFast estimated that emissions could exceed 20 million metric tons of CO₂e if its existing production operations in Vietnam reached their maximum registered capacity, excluding future factories. The estimate illustrates the importance of factoring energy efficiency, electricity sourcing and supplier emissions into plans for higher production. 

How the 3E Mission puts the 2040 pledge into practice

VinFast signed The Climate Pledge on August 17, 2022, and announced its participation in September 2022. It was the first Vietnamese enterprise to sign the pledge, an initiative co-founded by Amazon and Global Optimism. The company's stated goal is to reach net-zero emissions by 2040 across Scopes 1, 2 and 3, covering direct emissions from its operations, indirect emissions from purchased energy, and emissions across its wider value chain. Signatories commit to measuring and reporting greenhouse gas emissions regularly, reducing emissions and neutralizing the remainder.

In January 2025, VinFast's chairwoman approved the company's net-zero strategy through 2030, with a view to 2040. The strategy centers on the 3E Mission, which sets out how VinFast plans to change the equipment it uses, reduce the energy it needs and source cleaner power. 

  • Electrification. VinFast plans to electrify equipment at company-owned production and business sites by 2030. The roadmap also includes expanding access to charging and developing battery energy storage.
  • Energy Saving. VinFast plans to introduce smart energy monitoring at manufacturing facilities by 2028. Monitoring production lines and major electricity-consuming equipment gives factory teams more detailed information on where energy is used and where operations can be made more efficient.
  • Energy Greening. VinFast aims to use 100% renewable electricity at all its plants by 2040. Its roadmap includes rooftop solar, battery storage to support renewable power use, and work with suppliers on lower-emission materials.

VinFast's manufacturing complex in Hai Phong offers a practical example of what these priorities translate to on the factory floor. The company reported that upgrades to lighting and compressed-air systems, changes to how production robots operate, and other efficiency measures saved approximately 2.7 million kilowatt-hours of electricity in 2024, equivalent to an estimated 1,782 metric tons of CO₂e.

The company also said it initiated a 30-megawatt-peak rooftop solar project at the site. While the efficiency measures address how much electricity the plant needs, the solar project addresses the source of the electricity.

Against its 2022 baseline, VinFast aims to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 42% and Scope 3 emissions by 29% by 2030. By 2040, the strategy calls for cutting total emissions by at least 85% and neutralizing residual emissions of up to 15% through carbon offsetting mechanisms, which could include carbon credits. As VinFast serves more drivers and fleets, its reported emissions will show how far the company has progressed toward those targets across its operations, purchased energy and value chain.

DUBLIN, IE / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Great Western Mining Corporation PLC (AIM:GWMO)(Euronext Growth:8GW)(OTCQB:GWMOF), a strategic minerals exploration and development company, is pleased to provide an update on its Defender Tungsten Project ("Defender" or the "Project") in Mineral County, Nevada, USA, following the identification of a newly discovered adit approximately 400m west of the historical Widowmaker Mine. The Company has named this the Starry Night Mine ("Starry Night") and intends to prioritise sampling work there as part of its next phase of fieldwork in the coming weeks.

Starry Night Mine

Starry Night was identified by the Company's technical team during recent reconnaissance work at Defender and initial field observations, including shortwave ultraviolet ("SWUV") inspection, have identified approximately 50m of scheelite-bearing garnet skarn mineralisation along the adit.

As announced on 7 July 2026, it is theorised that a 3km skarn trend extends from the Defender Mine through the Pine Crow and Widowmaker Mines to the Company's JORC-compliant M2 skarn copper resource. As described in the Company's announcement of 18 August 2026, the Project comprises the historical Widowmaker, Pine Crow, Dough God and Defender tungsten mines, located along a >2km mineralised corridor within the total 3km mineralised trend running from Defender to the M2 resource.

Located west of Widowmaker, Starry Night has the potential to extend the Project's tungsten strike from approximately 2km to approximately 2.4km and lies along the 3km trend linking the Project to the M2 resource 600m away.

The Company intends to prioritise channel sampling at Starry Night and further updates will reported as results are received.

Figure 1: Location of the Starry Night Mine and extension of identified strike towards the M2 copper resource in the west.

Drill Assays and Maiden Mineral Resource Estimate

As announced on 23 September 2026, the Company completed a 23-hole reverse circulation drilling programme for approximately 8,500 ft (2,590 m) at Defender, with all samples dispatched to American Assay in Reno, Nevada. Assay results were expected in Q4 2026 however processing has since been delayed by laboratory capacity constraints affecting the region, and results are still outstanding.

Addison Mining Services ("Addison"), the independent Competent Person engaged to prepare the maiden JORC Mineral Resource Estimate ("MRE"), has been closely involved in the programme to date, including supervising the drilling. The Company therefore expects to be well positioned to progress the MRE promptly once assays are received.

Ed Loye, CEO of Great Western, commented: "Identifying Starry Night, a historical mine adit west of Widowmaker, is another very encouraging development for Defender. It has the potential to extend our tungsten strike to around 2.4km and adds a further valuable data point along the trend towards our M2 resource. We intend to prioritise sampling at Starry Night, and the team are keen to get on site as soon as possible, whilst noting winter weather conditions.

"The delay to our drill assays is frustrating, but not unique to Great Western. Laboratory capacity constraints are affecting the industry across the region and are a symptom of the current buoyant mining landscape in Nevada. Addison has been closely involved since before drilling began, which puts us in a good position to move quickly once results are received. The assays and maiden resource are expected to give us a much fuller picture of our opportunity at Defender as we look towards mine development."

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 26, 2026 / Panther Minerals Inc. ("Panther" or the "Company") (CSE:PURR)(OTCQB:GLIOF)(FWB:2BC) announces that it has elected to rely on Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 - Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers (the "Order") and move to semi-annual financial reporting ("SAR"). This news release is being filed pursuant to Coordinated Blanket Order 51 - 933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers.

The Order allows eligible venture issuers listed on the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE") to voluntarily move from a quarterly to a semi-annual financial reporting framework. The Company's fiscal year ends on June 30. Under the SAR pilot program, the Company will be exempt from filing interim financial reports and related Management's Discussion & Analysis (MD&A) for its first and third quarters.

  • Interim Period: The Company will not file an interim report for the first quarter (Q1) ending September 30 and the third quarter (Q3) ending March 31; and
  • Ongoing Reporting: The Company will continue to file audited financial statements (due within 120 days of June 30) and six-month interim financial reports (due within 60 days of December 31).

The Company confirms it meets the pilot program's eligibility criteria, which include being a venture issuer with annual revenues of no more than $10 million, having been a reporting issuer in at least one Canadian jurisdiction for at least 12 months and having ﬁled all required periodic and timely continuous disclosure documents.

The ﬁrst period for which the Company will not ﬁle an interim ﬁnancial report and related MD&A will be for the three-month period ended September 30, 2026.

About Panther Minerals Inc.

Panther Minerals Inc. is a North American critical minerals exploration company. Its portfolio includes the Rubidium Ridge lithium-cesium-tantalum property near Atikokan, Ontario, the East Brouillan property in Quebec, and an option to acquire a 100% interest in the Mesa Top uranium property in New Mexico. Panther trades on the CSE under the symbol PURR, on the OTCQB under the symbol GLIOF and on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under the symbol 2BC.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - BQE Water Inc. (TSXV: BQE), a leader in the treatment and management of mine impacted waters, is pleased to release its interim consolidated financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.

"With GAAP revenue up 32%, net income up 33% and Adjusted EBITDA up 38% over Q3 2025, our strong third quarter results allowed us to us to substantially narrow the gap on a year-to-date basis relative to the same period in 2025. In the third quarter, we remobilized our operations team back to the Kemess Mine, successfully restarting the treatment plant and operating it on a seasonal basis. We also initiated 3-year operations support for cyanide destruction for a facility in Alaska." said David Kratochvil, President & CEO of BQE Water. "We now have 26 treatment facilities across 11 operation sites in our recurring revenue portfolio. This growing operational base is supported by a strong pipeline of projects and opportunities that we expect to build on in the quarters ahead. In addition, we have good visibility into new near-term operating opportunities that are expected to allow us to redeploy our seasonal operations teams during the winter shutdown."

COMMENTARY AND OUTLOOK
We are pleased to have delivered strong third quarter results, with GAAP revenue up 32%, proportional revenue up 36%, net income up 33% and adjusted EBITDA up 38% over Q3 2025. In line with our previously communicated expectations, our strong third quarter results allowed us to us to substantially narrow the gap on a year-to-date basis relative to the same period in 2025.

Matching last year's Proportional Revenue on a year-to-date basis masks the strong underlying growth in our business. Recall that 2025 included a one-time revenue contract for the equipment sale, construction, design and commissioning of the Valley Tailings Facility, which was all recorded under technical services (advisory and design) revenue. Excluding the equipment sale component of $4.6 million from 2025, our year-to-date GAAP revenue increased 13% year-over-year, while our share of revenues from joint ventures in China also grew 38%. Although we are not eliminating the possibility of future equipment sales, the Company's business model is based on professional services linked to clean water production and our strategic focus is on our ability to grow our delivery of services, not equipment.

The primary driver of our growth in Q3 2026 and year-to-date has been recurring operations and short-term operations, which accounted for 81% and 77% of our Q3 2026 and year-to-date GAAP revenue, up from 67% and 59% in the comparable 2025 periods. In 2026, the Company operated a portfolio of 26 treatment facilities across 11 operation sites. On a year-to-date basis, new operations and support services contributed $4.6 million in additional revenue when compared to the same period in 2025. With respect to short-term operations, we added two facilities in 2026, while continuing temporary treatment at Eagle Mine. The Kemess treatment plant was recommissioned and operated for a few months in 2026, and, after a one-year hiatus, we also resumed operations at Minto Mine under a new arrangement with the new property owner, Selkirk Copper.

Excluding the above-noted equipment sale, our technical advisory and engineering services revenue has also grown but not to the same degree as our operations. We expect these services to increase gradually in Q4 2026 and into the first half of 2027 as our engineers currently undergoing site-based training to join our technical teams. All engineers hired in 2026 have been assigned to our operating sites for hands-on training before transitioning into technical teams in process design, field commissioning, or technology development. This approach is integral to the Company's vision of ensuring our technical staff develops practical field experience as a foundation for their professional growth.

Our year-to-date gross margin in dollar terms remained largely consistent at approximately $11.3 million (43.0%) compared to $11.6 million (41.4%) in the comparable prior period. The 33% decrease in year-to-date net income primarily reflects our continued investment in the people and systems required to support the Company's growth. In Q3 2026, our G&A expenses also included a one-time professional fee associated with the preparation and submission of SR&ED claims related to the Company's intellectual property and technology development activities in 2024, through which we generated $745,000 in non-refundable SR&ED investment tax credits that may be applied against future corporate income taxes payable. Moreover, under recently expanded federal and provincial SR&ED programs, the Company expects future qualifying claims for 2025 and beyond to generate refundable tax credits, providing a potential source of cash recoveries.

Our balance sheet remains strong, with working capital of $25.1 million at the end of Q3 2026, up $3.7 million from December 31, 2025. Our cash and cash equivalents stood at $17.6 million, down $1.3 million over this period, largely due to an increase in accounts receivable at the end of Q3 2026. In support of our future growth, we also invested $724,000 in capital assets during 2026, including mobile equipment at Britannia, leasehold improvements and laboratory equipment for the aquatic toxicology lab, as well as computer hardware and office equipment.

We continue to have long pipeline of projects and operations to build on the quarters ahead. While certain operations are seasonal and will pause over the winter, we have good visibility into new near-term operating opportunities that are expected to enable us to redeploy operation teams and continue generating operations revenue through the winter months. We also expect to commence several feasibility studies and a significant engineering design-for-construction project in the coming months, with anticipated project durations ranging from five to ten months.

Our growing pipeline provides strong visibility over the next 18 months. Our ability to execute on these opportunities will increasingly depend on expanding and successfully onboarding our technical team members. We will also continue to invest in and implement internal systems for accounting, safety management, and resource management to support a growing organization, resulting in additional near-term expenses. With mining industry activity remaining strong, we see a healthy environment for continued growth. We nevertheless remain mindful of geopolitical and market uncertainties and will maintain a disciplined approach to hiring, investment, and resource allocation to support profitable growth.

The Company, with our Inuit partner Nuvumiut Development, operates four water treatment plants at Raglan Mine for Glencore Canada Corporation ("Glencore"). The plants at Raglan Mine are usually shut down in the first quarter as water stored in the outdoor reservoirs is frozen. During Q3 2026, we continued treating water across all four plants for our 23rd operating season at the mine.

In 2021, we began providing operation support to two SART (sulphidization-acidification-recycling-thickening) plants at metallurgical facilities in Shandong province, China. In 2025, we commissioned the third SART plant in the same region. All three SART plants have been under our technical supervision since the start of production. During Q3 2026, our team provided ongoing technical supervision at two of the three plants as the Shandong Gold plant was shut down.

In 2022, we began operations of a treatment plant utilizing our Selen-IX™ process to remove selenium from ash pond water for WesTech Engineering ("WesTech"). In Q3 2026, our team continued on site, providing water treatment services with the Selen-IX™ circuit to manage the presence of selenium in the feed.

In 2022, we began operations of a treatment plant utilizing a combination of nanofiltration and our proprietary selenium electroreduction process for the simultaneous removal of selenium and sulphate from mine water for a base metal project in the American Southwest. In 2023, our team began operations for a second newly constructed selenium removal water treatment plant at the same site. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide onsite operations support and technical supervision at both treatment plants.

In October 2025, we completed the commissioning of a Selen-IX™ treatment plant located at the Coeur Wharf Mine in South Dakota and began providing routine operation support. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide onsite and offsite support to the selenium removal circuit to manage the presence of selenium in the feed.

In January 2026, we assumed operational responsibility for the provision of operations and maintenance services for the Britannia Mine water treatment plant for the BC government under a 20-year arrangement. This High-Density Sludge lime treatment plant neutralizes acidity and removes heavy metals, primarily copper and zinc, from the mine water collected in the legacy underground workings prior to its discharge into Howe Sound. In Q3 2026, our team continued to operate and treat water daily without interruption until August 2026 and carried out the annual shut-down maintenance in September 2026.

In February 2026, we initiated an annual operation support arrangement with an integrated lead smelter-recycling facility in Eastern Canada. Prior to this arrangement, we completed an upgrade to the existing treatment system, implemented a new sulphate removal stage to a discharge limit of less than 1,500 mg/L and provided short-term operations support for the newly upgraded facility. In Q3 2026, our team continued to provide ongoing site support and technical supervision.

In May 2026, we initiated a 3-year water treatment operations contract, with our Inuit partner Nuvumiut Development, to operate five treatment systems at the Nunavik Nickel Project owned by Canadian Royalties Inc. Treatment operations typically run from May to October depending on the volume of water requiring treatment. In Q3 2026, the operations team continued to operate across all five treatment systems.

In August 2026, we initiated a 3-year operations support contract to optimize a cyanide destruction circuit for a metallurgical facility in Alaska, USA. The support is intended to achieve consistent cyanide destruction performance, reducing reagent consumption, minimizing dilution water requirements, improving operational consistency between shifts, and ensuring effective implementation of the operating strategies and control philosophy. In Q3 2026, we mobilized our support team to support the facility.

SHORT-TERM OPERATIONS SERVICES HIGHLIGHTS

  • Continued operations at the ERDC Valley Tailings facility in the Yukon, which was constructed and commissioned last year.

  • Continued providing operations services at Minto Mine in the Yukon.

  • Initiated operations at the Kemess Mine water treatment plant in BC, which was the first selenium removal plant commissioned in 2020.

  • Demobilized our team from site services at Bell Mine in BC.

  • Continued to provide engineering design services for a water treatment system integrated into a rare earth extraction project in Brazil.

  • Completed engineering advisory services and restarted the selenium removal plant for short-term operations for the Kemess project in BC.

  • Completed a review of water treatment proposed for a new mine undergoing permitting in Yukon on behalf of the Yukon Government.

  • Initiated a pre-feasibility study engineering design for a plant to selectively recovery cobalt and scandium from copper heap leach solution in Chile.

  • Performed a review and assessment of opportunities to improve mine water treatment systems operations at legacy mines in Greece.

  • Performed a field assessment of selenium mitigation at a mine in Europe including a plan for implementing active treatment in the next 18 months.

Cyanide Management (Destruction and Recycle)

  • Completed engineering advisory services for cyanide destruction for a project in Australia.

  • Completed SART design for a new heap leach project in Mexico.

  • Continued providing engineering advisory services for estimating cyanide emissions, designing an emissions control system for cyanide, and revising engineering design of cyanide destruction for a project in the US.

  • Continued to provide plant engineering design services requiring an end-of-pipe cyanide level below 8 ppb to a project in the US.

  • Initiated field engineering advisory services for improving cyanide destruction performance at a mine in Alaska.

  • Continued detailed engineering for SART integration into the New Britannia mill in Manitoba, Canada.

Aquatic Toxicology Services

  • Continued assessment of chronic effects on aquatic environment caused by mine effluent at a mine in Western Canada.

  • Continued investigation into the effects of ammonia on acute toxicity under site-specific conditions at a mine in Eastern Canada.

  • Continued routine effluent toxicity quality monitoring for Eagle Mine water treatment operations and investigated the root cause of algae bloom.

  • Initiated laboratory tests required to establish a site-specific performance objective limit for sulphate and total dissolved solids at a mine in BC.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- DSC Holdings Ltd. (“DSC” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: DSC), the AI application infrastructure for China’s used car industry, today announced a vehicle-sourcing partnership with Japanese automotive trading company JAPANCARS CO., LTD. (“JAPANCARS”). The partnership went live on November 18, 2026, and is conducted through DASOUCHE PTE. LTD., the Company’s Singapore-based overseas headquarters. JAPANCARS operates JAPANCARS Exporter Platform, a vehicle export marketplace serving dealers worldwide. Through the partnership, JAPANCARS and its dealer clients can tap directly into the vast inventory offered by Chinese used car dealers, marking a significant step in DSC’s effort to connect China’s used car supply with global distribution networks.

For China’s used car industry, this partnership builds a direct and efficient route to overseas markets. China’s massive used car supply is spread across several hundred thousand dealers, nearly all of which are small and mid-sized independent businesses, which makes cross-border used car trades difficult and inefficient. Few dealers have reliable relationships with overseas buyers, and most lack the standardized vehicle data, language capabilities and fulfillment capacity that cross-border trade demands. As a long-time partner to China’s used car dealers, DSC aims to remove those barriers. Its platform gives dealers a consolidated point of entry to overseas marketplaces, allowing them to reach buyers worldwide without painstakingly building export channels of their own. The result is a shift from piecemeal, one-to-one transactions to a scaled channel connecting hundreds of thousands of Chinese dealers with buyers around the world. This partnership with JAPANCARS is expected to contribute to DSC’s digitalization solutions revenue and drive demand for related transaction services.

JAPANCARS has built a well-established automotive trading business spanning Japan, Southeast Asia and North America, serving more than 2,500 dealers in 46 countries to date. International dealers seeking to purchase inventory across multiple Chinese sellers have typically needed to reach out to each of the sellers separately. This partnership with DSC gives JAPANCARS’ worldwide clients one place to browse China’s deep pool of vehicle inventory and source the models that suit their local demand.

“International expansion is a clear, long-term strategy for DSC,” said Liyu Zhang, Senior Vice President of DSC. “Teaming up with JAPANCARS to bring high-quality Chinese used cars to overseas buyers is an encouraging start. We will keep equipping our dealers to sell abroad, smoothing their path into international markets, and helping China’s used cars build a strong presence worldwide.”

“Used car exports hinge on understanding overseas demand and local pricing,” said Terry On, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of JAPANCARS. “Through our partnership with DSC, we act as a conduit, helping overseas buyers find the right Chinese used cars for their markets while showing Chinese dealers which models can sell abroad.”

About DSC

DSC is the AI application infrastructure for China’s used car industry. Since 2021, DSC has consistently held more than 90% market share in operating systems for China’s used car dealers, according to CIC, giving it deep connections with dealers nationwide and exclusive access to massive, granular, real-time industry data. Building on this digital infrastructure, DSC provides used car dealers with essential transaction services across their workflows. DSC’s platform also engages and benefits thousands of dealer collaborators, including used car inspectors, transporters and other internet platform service providers, forming an ecosystem with used car dealers at its center.

About JAPANCARS

Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Kanagawa Prefecture, JAPANCARS is a B2B exporter and trader of new and used vehicles, serving customers worldwide from its base in Japan. Its JAPANCARS Exporter Platform gives clients direct access to used car auctions, where they can choose from tens of thousands of vehicles on offer each day, with JAPANCARS supporting them through bidding, condition inspection and shipping.

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Hertz Energy Inc. (CSE: HZ) (OTCQB: HZLIF) (FSE: A340) ("Hertz" or the "Company") announces that it has amended the terms of its non-brokered private placement previously announced on October 9, 2026 (the "Offering").

The Company has replaced the charity flow-through units with critical minerals flow-through units and traditional flow-through units, and has reduced the size of the non-flow-through portion of the Offering, as described below. Coloured Ties Capital Inc., whose participation in the Offering was announced on October 15, 2026, will not be participating in the amended Offering.

Amended Offering

CRITICAL MINERALS FLOW-THROUGH UNITS

The gross proceeds from the sale of Lake George FT Units will be used for exploration at the Company's Lake George antimony-tungsten project in New Brunswick, and the gross proceeds from the sale of Craig FT Units will be used for exploration at the Company's Craig silver project in Yukon. Net Revenue Up 6% in the Third Quarter; System Sales Exceed $8M in a Quarter; Company Makes Multiple Growth Investments in Q3, Including New Studio Opening and Acquisition

Boston, MA, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MiniLuxe Holding Corp. (TSXV: MNLX) today announced its financial results for the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 27, 2026 (“Q3 2026” and “YTD 2026”, respectively). The comparative prior year periods are the 13 weeks and 39 weeks ended September 28, 2025.

MiniLuxe is on a mission to make self-care something you can feel good about, starting with your nails. The Company delivers premium nail care in studios known for hospital-grade hygiene, cleaner polishes, and treatments that are better for you and for the people who provide them. What sets MiniLuxe apart is its people and culture, which are at the center of its competitive advantage. In an industry infamous for churn and poor working conditions, MiniLuxe has retained 86% of its hourly workforce on average over each of the last three years. Team members who are with the Company five years or more receive stock options, giving them a stake in the Company’s success, along with real career paths. Today, more than half of MiniLuxe’s service professionals (nail designers and waxing specialists) have reached that milestone.

The third quarter of 2026 delivered another quarter of year-over-year growth, with total Company net revenue up 6.1% to $7.7M and system sales up 8% to $8.1M from $7.5M in Q3 2025. Growth was driven by continued same-studio sales gains in both volume and mix. System sales include sales from all MiniLuxe studios, including franchised locations. The quarter extends a long, unbroken run of year-over-year revenue growth, reflecting continued demand for MiniLuxe services.

The Company made multiple growth investments in the third quarter: new studios, new AI-driven, geo-targeted paid marketing tests, upgrades to existing studios, and additional nail designer hours ahead of the fourth-quarter holiday season, its period of peak demand. While these initiatives resulted in some short-term margin pullback, management expects them to deliver meaningful returns over the longer term. After the quarter ended, the Company also put in place its first price increase in approximately three years, of approximately 5%, which management expects to more than offset rising labor and health care benefit costs.

  • New studios: The Company opened its Mansfield, Massachusetts joint-venture studio on July 30 and acquired a majority interest in an existing studio in Burlington, Massachusetts on September 4. The third quarter was also the first full quarter for the new MiniLuxe Lakewood studio in Dallas.
  • Marketing tests: Early results are encouraging, with some test studios attracting record numbers of new clients who are also returning faster for repeat visits.
  • Studio upgrades: The Company began renovating several existing studios with new dual stations that allow a manicure and pedicure at the same time. In the first studios, these stations cost at least 50% less than legacy stations, and productivity per station has been as much as double that of legacy pedicure stations.
  • Nail designer hours: Staffed hours were up 7% over the prior year, which positions the Company well for fourth-quarter demand.

 MiniLuxe’s Focus and Key Strategic Pillars in Q3 2026

The Company continued to make meaningful progress across each of its core strategic pillars in the third quarter of fiscal 2026:

  1. Attract, develop and retain high-quality nail designer talent;
  2. Drive growth through operating partners and franchise partners;
  3. Accelerate overall studio-level profitability and drive overall Company profitability;
  4. Strengthen balance sheet with sufficient capital to execute against growth plans.

Management Commentary

We also increased total nail designer hours and put marketing tests in place to attract new customers. We are already seeing early results as we attract new customers and see repeat visits, and we believe these investments will deliver a significant return over the medium to longer term. One of the most noteworthy statistics for me is that about half of our customer base is now Gen Z, which bodes well for the longevity of our brand and customer lifetime value.” – Tony Tjan, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer

Adjusted EBITDA

Management believes Adjusted EBITDA most accurately reflects the commercial reality of the Company’s operations on an ongoing basis by adding back non-cash expenses. Additionally, the rent-related adjustments ensure that studio-related expenses align with revenue generated over the corresponding time periods.

Adjusted EBITDA is calculated by adding back fixed asset depreciation, right-of-use asset amortization under IFRS 16, asset disposal, and share-based compensation expense to IFRS operating income, then deducting cash rent expenses net of lease abatements. When relevant, we will add back adjustments made to the P&L as a result of accounting policies that are non-cash or do not have operational impacts (for example, inventory adjustments or deferred revenue). IFRS operating income is revenue less cost of sales (gross profit), additionally adjusted for general and administrative expenses, and depreciation and amortization expenses. Normalized Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as Adjusted EBITDA, further adjusted to (i) remove items that management considers one-time or not representative of ongoing operations, and (ii) present the comparative period on a basis consistent with the current period. Management uses Normalized Adjusted EBITDA to assess the Company’s run-rate operating performance. It should be read together with, and not as a substitute for, operating loss and Adjusted EBITDA.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - NTG Clarity Networks Inc. (TSXV: NCI) (OTC Pink: NYWKF) ("NTG" or the "Company") today reported its financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All figures are in Canadian dollars.

Q3 2026 Highlights

Comparisons are to the quarter ended September 30, 2025 unless otherwise stated.

  • Revenue: was $19.2M, down 7.9% year-over-year from $20.9M and down 4.3% from $20.1M in Q2 2026. The sequential decline has narrowed in each quarter of 2026 as the situation in the middle east shows early signs of stability. Year-to-date revenue is up approximately 2% year-over-year to $60.6M compared to $59.4M in 2025.

  • Gross Profit: was $6.3M or 33.0% of revenue, compared to $7.3M or 34.9%, reflecting pricing concessions on renewals.

  • Net Income: Total comprehensive income was $0.2M or 1.0% of revenue, compared to $1.9M or 9.1%, reflecting lower operating leverage in the quarter. NTG's delivery capacity is its strongest asset and keeping it in place, as discussed in Q2, allows us to take advantage of new opportunities.

  • Adjusted EBITDA: was $0.6M or 2.9% of revenue, compared to $2.5M or 11.9% in 2025, and compared to approximately nil in Q2 2026. Revenue was $0.9M lower than in Q2 2026 and the cost base was $1.4M lower.

  • Operating Cash Flow: of $3.2M, compared to an outflow of $3.3M in Q3 2025 and an outflow of $4.6M in Q2 2026. Cash was $3.4M at September 30, 2026, compared to $2.8M at June 30, 2026.

  • Purchase Orders: $33.4M announced in Q3 2026, or 1.7 times revenue, compared to $12.3M in Q2 2026

"We are seeing early signs of stability, both in the wider Saudi economy, where GDP recovered slightly from Q2, and in purchase order activity from our clients," said Adam Zaghloul, Vice President of Strategy & Planning at NTG Clarity. "Purchase orders were $33.4 million in the third quarter and we have announced a further $24.5 million since. Our focus now is staffing those orders and turning them into billings. Collections improved in the quarter, bringing receivables and unbilled contract assets down, and that progress has continued into the fourth quarter. We have worked with our clients on pricing and billing through a difficult period, and we believe that is how long-term relationships in the Kingdom are built."

Fiscal 2026 Financial Outlook

The prolonged conflict in the Middle East has disrupted oil shipments through the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea, on which many digitization initiatives in Saudi Arabia and the rest of the Gulf rely for funding. Saudi enterprises have responded with a focus on cost savings and return on investment. Some customers have negotiated more favourable pricing, paused expansion and in some cases scaled back their engagements.

Revenue declined again in Q3 as these adjustments took effect. However, order intake has been steadier, starting in Q3 and extending into the fourth quarter, with an increased pace of new purchase orders, a four-year extension of an existing framework agreement and a new three-year framework agreement with a new customer. NTG has worked with its customers through this period on pricing, on billing terms and on the size of their engagements. The Company believes that supporting its customers during these difficult conditions strengthens its standing in the region. The new framework agreement announced on November 17, 2026 marks the fourth portfolio company of one of the Kingdom's largest investment entities to become an NTG customer and is a sign of the growing position of NTG within some of the most prestigious companies in the region.

Management is continually evaluating the prospects for future growth against its delivery capacity with an eye towards cash generation and improving profitability. NTG's top priority is cash collections and receivables management so that it remains self-funded during the turbulence in the Middle East. Q3 showed progress, with an overall reduction in accounts receivable due to strong collections and no bad debts expected. Those collections continued into Q4, which showed receivables decreasing by approximately a further $4M by the end of October.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ero Copper Corp. (TSX: ERO, NYSE: ERO) ("Ero" or the "Company") announces that all production activities, including mining and processing, at the Tucumã Operation have been temporarily suspended in compliance with a notice from the Pará State Environment and Sustainability Secretariat ("SEMAS").

Last week, the Tucumã Operation experienced significant rainfall events stemming from this year's very strong El Niño conditions, which overwhelmed the pumping capacity of a surface contact-water sump and resulted in two localized overflow events. The rainfall events were short in duration but included peaks above 70mm per hour. Significant rain events contributed to overall rainfall in the first 20 days of November that totaled approximately 275mm, as measured at the operation's weather station, approximately 170% above normal seasonal rainfall for the entire month of November. Upon identifying the overflow events, the Company promptly activated additional resources to increase water pumping and storage capacity along with relocating a stockpile to reduce the potential for additional contact water in the area affected by the overflows. The Company also notified SEMAS of the overflow events.

SEMAS conducted an independent technical assessment of the overflow events and notified the Company that it had identified anomalous pH readings in local water samples near the Tucumã Operation. SEMAS directed the Company to temporarily suspend mining operations; however, processing operations were permitted to continue while the Company engaged in active and constructive dialogue with SEMAS regarding continuity of mining and processing operations concurrent with remediation and planning efforts.

Despite stoppage of all production activities, constructive dialogue remains ongoing, and the Company expects to submit the final remediation plan requested by SEMAS for its review shortly. The Tucumã Operation is expected to resume activities following SEMAS's technical review and subsequent approval of the Company's proposed remediation plan. Fines associated with the overflow events totaled approximately US$2.9 million (BRL $16.8 million).

Weather conditions in October and this month have significantly impacted Pará State. Communities in and near the municipality of São Félix do Xingu, located approximately 50 km away from the Tucumã Operation, reported two separate fish mortality events prior to the aforementioned overflow events. The São Félix do Xingu municipal environment secretariat has issued a fine associated with these fish mortality events totaling approximately US$1.9 million (BRL $10.9 million). To date, Ero has not received documentation to support this fine, and no correlation between these events and the Tucumã Operation has been identified by Ero. The Company is working collaboratively with the technical agencies responsible for mining activities in the region.

Ero remains fully committed to remediation of the areas impacted by the overflow events, protecting the environment and contributing responsibly to the region.

ABOUT ERO

Ero is a Brazil-focused, growth-oriented mining company with a diversified portfolio of copper and gold assets. Headquartered in Vancouver, B.C., the Company operates two copper mines – the Caraíba Operations in Bahia State and the Tucumã Operation in Pará State – as well as the Xavantina Operations, a producing gold mine in Mato Grosso State. In addition to its operating assets, Ero is advancing the Furnas Copper-Gold Project, located in the mineral-rich Carajás Province in Pará State, through a definitive earn-in agreement with Vale Base Metals to acquire a 60% interest in the project.

Ero’s operating philosophy is grounded in a commitment to safety, operational excellence, and the responsible production of minerals essential for a better tomorrow. The Company’s shares are publicly traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol “ERO.” Additional information, including technical reports on the Company’s operations and projects, is available on the Company’s website (www.ero.com), SEDAR+ (www.sedarplus.ca), and on EDGAR (www.sec.gov).

Delta, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Fab-Form Industries Ltd. (TSXV: FBF) ("Fab-Form" or the "Company") announced today its financial results for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, the first quarter of fiscal 2027. All amounts are in Canadian dollars unless otherwise stated.

Financial Highlights

Against the backdrop of a soft Canadian construction market and the Company's first quarter of direct operations in Missouri, the Company reports:

  • Revenue for the first quarter decreased 7.52% to $1,367,898 compared to $1,479,187 in the quarter ended 30 September 2025, mainly due to declines in Nudura Insulated Concrete Forms ("ICF") sales (-18.71%), the Company's largest product line, Helix (-85.83%), ICF accessories (-69.96%) and Monopour (-14.36%). The decrease was partially offset by growth in Bracing (+51.73%), Fast-Tube® (+94.07%) and Fastfoot® (+16.37%) sales. The growth in Bracing and Fastfoot® was mainly due to the establishment of the Company's Missouri operations.

  • Gross profit increased 2.11% to $533,349 from $522,333, and gross margin improved to 39.0% from 35.3%. Cost of sales fell 12.78%, faster than revenue, reflecting a shift in sales mix towards higher margin products, lower sales of low margin products and the contribution from Missouri.

  • Operating expenses increased 15.57% to $290,980. General and administrative expenses rose 28.77% to $233,319, mainly due to higher wages and benefits (+40.09%) and research and development expenses (+84.57%), while selling and marketing expenses fell 18.31% to $57,661.

  • Earnings from operations declined 10.42% to $242,369, compared to $270,553 in the same quarter last year. Operating margin was 17.7% compared to 18.3%.

  • Other income fell 95.20% to $2,246, compared to $46,840 in the same quarter last year, following the retirement of a short-term investment to acquire property in White Rock.

  • Net earnings for the quarter were $179,945 ($0.020 per share), down 24.21% from $237,434 ($0.026 per share) in the same quarter last year.

Financial Position

  • As of 30 September 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $1,788,621, up $193,280 (12.1%) from $1,595,341 at 30 June 2026 and up $451,912 (33.8%) from $1,336,709 at 30 September 2025.

  • Net cash generated from operating activities was $329,548 (2025: $362,982). Cash of $123,932 was used in investing activities, comprising property and equipment ($17,391), product development ($47,001) and intangible assets ($59,540). Cash of $30,566 was used in financing activities for lease payments on the Delta, BC office and warehouses.

  • Total assets grew to $7,844,954 from $7,436,824 at 30 June 2026, and shareholders' equity increased to $6,497,998 from $6,318,053.

  • The Company has no long-term debt other than lease liabilities, with total liabilities of $1,346,956, ensuring financial stability and flexibility for future growth.

Product and Market Update

Fab-Form continues to focus on its core product lines while advancing innovative solutions in concrete forming technology. Highlights for the quarter include:

U.S. Expansion - Missouri Branch

The Missouri branch generated revenue of $306,003 in its first quarter of operations, representing 22.4% of Company revenue. Its gross profit was $186,050, a gross margin of 60.8%, and it contributed 34.9% of Company gross profit. The decision to operate directly in Missouri responds to U.S. tariffs, the need for shorter delivery times for U.S. customers and a soft Canadian construction market. Tariffs are now paid only on steel costs rather than on selling prices, reducing the Company's exposure. Tariffs are expected to remain a challenge for steel exports to the U.S., and any further changes could affect steel product sales growth.

The Missouri location provides quick access to all U.S. states, supports distributors and contractors, and ties into the Company's target of US$3 million in additional revenue within 24 months. It also provides a base to introduce Fast-Tube® 3.0, Space-R™, Flex-R™, Ever-Wall™ and Zuckle™ 2XK into the U.S. market.

Fast-Tube®

Fast-Tube® sales almost doubled, rising 94.07% to $82,224. In late September, a record test pour was completed at the Company's Springfield, Missouri warehouse, in which a 40-foot Fast-Tube® column was poured in just 70 minutes, a speed the Company believes no other forming system can match, and which demonstrates the pouring advantages Fast-Tube® offers contractors over cardboard tubes.

New Patent Applications and Zuckle™ 2XK

During the quarter the Company applied for two new patents, Ever-Wall™ and Zuckle 2XK™.

The Company also completed the design and specification of the new version of its drill adjustable wall aligner, Zuckle 2XK. Production of the first batch began shortly after quarter end, and the product is expected to be available to customers in mid-February 2027 from both the Delta, BC and Missouri locations. Recent test profiles show a load capacity approaching 13,000 lb, and the product has been engineered for low-cost production.

Agreement with 12 British Columbia First Nations marks another milestone in Indigenous participation in Canadian energy infrastructure

CALGARY, Alberta, Nov. 26, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- TC Energy Corporation (TSX, NYSE: TRP) (TC Energy or the Company) today announced the closing of an agreement with CGL First Nations Limited Partnership (CGL FNLP), an Indigenous-led investment entity representing 12 First Nations along the Coastal GasLink (CGL) corridor, including Cheslatta Carrier Nation; Kitselas First Nation; Lheidli T’enneh First Nation; Nadleh Whut’en First Nation, Nee Tahi Buhn Indian Band; Saik’uz First Nation; Skin Tyee Nation; Stellat'en First Nation; Ts’il Kaz Koh First Nation; Wet’suwet’en First Nation; Witset First Nation; and Yekooche First Nation.

Through the agreement, participating Nations have acquired an economic interest in the entity that holds TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL. These communities are expected to benefit from long-term predictable financial returns associated with TC Energy’s limited partner interest in CGL.

This transaction marks the second Indigenous investment involving TC Energy's interest in CGL and reflects years of partnership with Indigenous communities along the corridor.

Creating opportunities through partnership
“This transaction demonstrates what is possible when Indigenous communities, industry and governments come together with a shared commitment to creating opportunities that deliver benefits over the long term,” said François Poirier, President and Chief Executive Officer of TC Energy. “It reflects the strength of the relationships developed along the Coastal GasLink corridor over more than a decade of collaboration and our shared belief that major projects should create lasting value for the communities connected to them.”

“This investment represents a historic milestone for our Nations and a new chapter in our relationship with Coastal GasLink,” said Corrina Leween, Director & Executive Committee member, CGL FNLP. “It reflects years of work to advance Indigenous participation in major infrastructure projects and to create a stronger role for our Nations in shaping the economic future of our territories. Through this transaction, our Nations will benefit from a long-term economic interest that provides stable, predictable returns for our communities, helping support future generations and strengthen our collective prosperity. Today’s achievement would not have been possible without the vision and leadership of the late Niilo Edwards, whose commitment to Indigenous economic empowerment helped bring our Nations together around this opportunity.”

Expanding pathways to participation
This transaction was supported by a loan guarantee made available under the Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Program, administered by the Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Corporation (CILGC).

“We commend TC Energy for working with CGL First Nations Limited Partnership to advance this investment. Partnerships like this can support a more inclusive approach to infrastructure development while strengthening Indigenous economic self-determination and creating opportunities for Nations to share in long-term, project benefits,” said Kristan Straub, President and CEO, Canada Indigenous Loan Guarantee Corporation.

“At a time when Canada must build big things again, in partnership with Indigenous Peoples, projects like Coastal GasLink are helping us strengthen our economic sovereignty, diversify our trade, advance reconciliation and Indigenous prosperity, and secure our place as a global energy superpower. By combining Indigenous economic participation with the investment certainty needed to advance major projects, we are responsibly driving Canada's next generation of growth,” said the Honourable Tim Hodgson, Minister of Energy and Natural Resources.

“Economic reconciliation is about ensuring that Indigenous communities have the opportunity to own, invest in, and benefit from the major projects shaping Canada’s future. This investment will support 12 First Nations in acquiring an interest in, and derive meaningful long-term benefits from, one of Canada’s most important energy infrastructure projects. By helping unlock Indigenous ownership in major projects, we are creating opportunities to build long-term wealth, generate sustainable revenues, and advance economic self-determination for generations to come,” said the Honourable François-Philippe Champagne, Minister of Finance and National Revenue.

Building on more than a decade of partnership
For many participating Nations, this agreement represents the next chapter in a relationship with CGL that spans more than a decade.

The investment opportunity was made available to all 20 Indigenous communities with existing CGL agreements. Participation reflects the independent decisions of each Nation based on its own priorities and objectives.

On Oct. 13, 2026, TC Energy announced its first Indigenous investment agreement related to CGL, involving participating Nations represented through FN CGL Pipeline Limited Partnership. Together, the two agreements build on years of partnership and create additional opportunities for Indigenous communities to benefit from the long-term financial returns associated with TC Energy's limited partner interest in CGL.

A critical pathway for Canadian LNG exports
As operator and co-owner of CGL, TC Energy safely delivers 2.1 billion cubic feet per day of Canadian natural gas to LNG Canada in Kitimat, B.C., supporting Canadian LNG exports to global markets. With the announcement of CGL Phase 2, system capacity will nearly double, demonstrating the growing global demand for natural gas and long-term value of Canadian LNG exports.

Transaction advisors
RBC Capital Markets acted as financial advisor to TC Energy and Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP as legal counsel.

For CGL First Nations Limited Partnership, National Bank of Canada Capital Markets acted as business and financial advisors, and Gowling WLG acted as legal counsel.

About TC Energy
We are a leader in North American energy infrastructure, spanning Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. For over 75 years, we have proudly connected the world to the energy it needs. Every day, we move more than 30 per cent of the natural gas used across the continent and connect LNG exports to global markets—powering communities and industries. Complemented by strategic ownership and low-risk investments in power generation, our infrastructure delivers affordable, reliable and sustainable energy across North America. 

We carry forward a legacy of nation building energy infrastructure and strong partnerships. By working with communities, businesses and leaders across our extensive energy network, we create opportunities today and for generations to come. 

TC Energy’s common shares trade on the Toronto (TSX) and New York (NYSE) stock exchanges under the symbol TRP. To learn more, visit us at TCEnergy.com.

About Coastal GasLink
CGL is Canada’s first direct pathway to global LNG export markets. It is a 670-kilometre (416-mile) natural gas pipeline that safely delivers 2.1 Bcf/d of natural gas from northeastern British Columbia to the LNG Canada facility in Kitimat, B.C., where it is liquefied for export to global markets. The infrastructure is owned by Coastal GasLink Pipeline Limited Partnership, with TC Energy as the operator.

About CGL First Nations Limited Partnership
CGL First Nations Limited Partnership comprises of 12 First Nations that will collectively hold an economic interest in the entity holding TC Energy’s limited partner interest in the Coastal GasLink project. The partnership was established to pursue collective economic opportunities and advance Indigenous ownership in the Coastal GasLink project, creating long-term benefits for participating Nations and future generations.
